article_hits.content: Lego marketplace BrickLink offline after 'unusual activity' detected Image source, Reuters Image caption, The marketplace is sometimes called the 'eBay' of Lego By Zoe Kleinman Technology editor Published 28 minutes ago Lego has taken its online marketplace BrickLink offline after detecting what it described as unusual activity on the platform. BrickLink is used by Lego collectors worldwide to buy and sell secondhand Lego sets, source new bricks and purchase limited edition releases. It was originally set up by a fan, but Lego acquired it in 2019. In a homepage message, the firm said that before restoring BrickLink, it wanted to "fully understand" what had happened. "That means containing the issue, investigating how it happened and checking for related issues," Lego said. It did not provide any further detail about whether the site has been breached or hacked, and whether any customer data was affected. After being contacted by the BBC, Lego published the update. article_hits.title: Faster Retrieval for Better, More Efficient RAG
article_hits.content: content type highlight published November 5, 2026 Faster Retrieval for Better, More Efficient RAG Maximum inner product search (MIPS) sits at the core of recommendation systems, search, and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). Given a query vector, MIPS systems search within a database of millions of candidate key vectors for the one that best matches the query. The original data point associated with that best-matching key is then used to handle the query: in RAG, the document that is best suited to answer the question is typically prefixed to the query. As the number of keys grows to millions and vector dimensions reach thousands, the computational cost of running an exhaustive comparison of the query to all keys grows dramatically. Numerous approximate methods have been proposed to trade off accuracy for speed using clustering and quantization.
